/exhibition-stand-design-dubai.description: Exhibition stand design in Dubai: plan the layout, product displays, graphics and 3D concept brief, review real FANN stands and agree the build scope.
/exhibition-stand-design-dubai.heading: Exhibition stand design in Dubai
/exhibition-stand-design-dubai.subheading: A practical route from your Dubai stand allocation to layout, concept visuals and a clearly defined build proposal.
/exhibition-stand-design-dubai.intro: FANN designs and builds exhibition stands in Dubai, supported by an office in Al Barsha 1 and a joinery workshop in Umm Al Quwain. Start the design with your stand allocation, products and visitor needs. Agree the layout, visual direction and required design deliverables before construction details are released. The completed Dubai stands below are real project references. They show layouts and visible features, not guaranteed visitor results or venue appointment.
/exhibition-stand-design-dubai.heroAlt: Geven aircraft seating stand at Aircraft Interiors Middle East, Dubai, 2025, designed and built by FANN, with LED perimeter and product seating displays
/exhibition-stand-design-dubai.heroCaption: Completed FANN project: Geven at Aircraft Interiors Middle East, Dubai, 2025. A design and build reference for product-led layouts; it does not establish a venue appointment or measured visitor result.

sections.heading: Turn the allocation into a stand design brief
sections.text: Share the show, venue, hall, floor plan, stand dimensions and open sides. Identify the products or equipment being displayed, demonstrations, meetings, reception and storage. Add brand guidelines and the current exhibitor manual. The design should answer this brief rather than reuse a layout drawn for another exhibitor.

sections.heading: Plan the visitor route and product display together
sections.text: Decide what visitors should notice from the aisle and where they can stop without blocking the entrance. Place product displays, meeting areas, reception and storage around the allocation. Confirm product dimensions, handling and access needs before finalising counters or display furniture.

sections.heading: Agree what the 3D concept includes
sections.text: Specify the views, layout information, branding and material direction needed to review the concept. Identify which decisions are still provisional and who approves them. Concept visuals explain the appearance and arrangement; technical drawings, engineering and venue submissions are separate deliverables unless the agreed scope includes them.

sections.heading: Check graphics, lighting and equipment interfaces
sections.text: Review artwork against the actual panel sizes and joins, then coordinate screens, furniture, lighting and equipment with the layout. Identify power, data and other service responsibilities in the brief. Do not infer print dimensions, electrical loads or structural details from a rendered image.

sections.heading: Move from approved design to an itemised build scope
sections.text: Confirm the agreed drawing revision, materials, graphics, production, transport, installation and dismantling. Identify venue submissions, service orders, support and storage as included, excluded or supplied by others. Later revisions need their effect on scope, price and programme confirmed before the changed work is released.

sections.heading: Confirm the open sides before comparing design options
sections.text: Read the allocated plan together with the dimensions and orientation, then confirm which edges face the aisle. Mark product access, reception and meeting needs on that plan before choosing a visual direction. A layout drawn for a different set of open sides may place a counter, wall or display where your visitors need to enter.
items: Allocation: record the hall, stand number, dimensions and aisle-facing edges.
Options: compare the same products, meeting needs, storage and brand message in every layout.
Decision: name the person selecting the direction and identify what still needs a technical check.

sections.heading: Use a design review to make decisions, not collect renders
sections.text: Ask what each option changes: the visitor route, product position, meeting privacy, storage or visible branding. Select the useful elements and record one agreed direction. Keep the reference images separate from the production instruction, and mark any dimensions, materials, lighting or equipment that remain provisional.

sections.heading: Keep the selected option tied to the quote and artwork
sections.text: Before releasing fabrication, compare the selected layout and drawing revision with the itemised proposal. Confirm the stand elements, finish direction, graphic locations and interfaces that the quoted work includes. Keep a record of later changes so an approved visual is not mistaken for approval of every service, material substitution or extra item.

faqs.question: What do you need for exhibition stand design in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Send the show and venue, floor plan, stand dimensions and open sides, product information, planned activities and brand assets. Include the current exhibitor manual and required dates. Identify meetings, reception, storage, demonstrations and equipment. FANN can then review the layout and design deliverables against your actual allocation and brief.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a stand concept and a build-ready design?
faqs.answer: A concept communicates layout, appearance, branding and proposed materials. A build-ready package needs the drawings, specifications, service coordination and specialist inputs required for the actual structure and show. Agree those deliverables separately. A polished 3D image is not a structural calculation, construction specification or guarantee that the venue will approve it.

faqs.question: Can we review real Dubai exhibition stand designs?
faqs.answer: Yes. The linked Geven, TREVOS and Bayara galleries are existing FANN Dubai project references. Use the visible layouts, counters, displays and brand features to explain your preferences. A photograph does not establish a material specification, visitor result or the scope appropriate for your next stand; those details need separate agreement.

faqs.question: How are design revisions and production coordinated?
faqs.answer: Name the person approving layouts and artwork, and agree the design deliverables and revision allowance. Record the drawing revision released for production. Changes to dimensions, materials, equipment or graphics need their effect on scope, price, approvals and timing checked before the changed work proceeds. No unlimited or automatically free revisions are promised.

faqs.question: Who handles Dubai venue drawings and submission deadlines?
faqs.answer: Submission and service responsibilities are agreed for the project using the current show and venue manuals. Identify who prepares drawings, provides specialist inputs, submits them and answers comments. FANN undertakes the agreed scope, not an unconditional approval guarantee. The organiser schedule and actual design determine the requirements and deadlines.

faqs.question: Why do open sides matter when choosing a stand layout?
faqs.answer: Open sides determine where visitors can approach and where walls, counters and displays can sit. Confirm the aisle-facing edges on your allocated plan before comparing options. The same footprint with different open sides is a different design brief, so a reference image should not override the booking or agreed access needs.

faqs.question: How should we compare several stand design options?
faqs.answer: Compare every option against the same products, visitor activities, meeting needs, storage and brand message. Look at the entry route and equipment positions, not only the render style. Record the useful elements and choose one direction for development, with unresolved dimensions, materials and service requirements clearly identified before the next approval.

faqs.question: Can we send reference images with our stand allocation?
faqs.answer: Yes, send reference images alongside your allocated plan and explain which features you like, such as an entrance, display wall, meeting area or colour direction. References help communicate preferences; they do not establish a construction specification, permission to copy another design, or suitability for your venue and actual product requirements.

faqs.question: What should be checked after selecting a design option?
faqs.answer: Check the selected layout against the stand allocation and itemised proposal, then record the current drawing and artwork revisions. Confirm dimensions, product interfaces, materials, graphic locations and the services included in the quote. Identify outstanding technical or venue inputs before releasing affected work, rather than assuming the selected image settles every detail.

faqs.question: Can layout and artwork changes affect the build scope?
faqs.answer: Yes. A moved display, larger screen, revised counter or new graphic can affect dimensions, materials, service connections or work already released. Describe the requested change against the current drawing revision and confirm its effect on scope, price and programme before proceeding. The original concept does not grant unlimited revisions or automatic approval.

/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.description: Planning a medical centre in Dubai? Build a room-by-room fit-out brief, compare scope and approval duties, and see FANN healthcare projects.
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.heading: Medical centre fit-out in Dubai
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.subheading: Plan a multi-room healthcare fit-out around the service brief, room schedule and responsibilities before pricing.
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.intro: A medical centre is more than a collection of consulting rooms. Reception, patient routes, staff areas and room services need to work together. FANN is a Dubai design and build company with an in-house joinery workshop in Umm Al Quwain. Start your medical-centre fit-out enquiry with the planned services, site information and room schedule so the proposed work can be defined and priced. Clinical planning and licensing decisions remain with the operator and the appointed qualified specialists.
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.heroAlt: Aspris Clinic City Walk reception photograph from the FANN portfolio
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.heroCaption: Aspris Clinic - City Walk: a healthcare project in the FANN portfolio. The photograph is a reception reference, not evidence of regulatory approval or the scope of every trade.
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.proofHeading: Healthcare projects in the FANN portfolio
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.proposalHeading: Request a scoped medical-centre fit-out proposal
/medical-centre-fit-out-dubai.proposalText: Share the location, available drawings, planned services, room list and target opening date. Identify the operator, design consultant and any specialist equipment suppliers. Agree the responsibilities and exclusions before work is committed.

sections.heading: Start with the clinical service brief, not a finish palette
sections.text: Define what the centre will provide and who will use it. A polyclinic with several specialities needs a different room schedule from a single-practitioner clinic. The DHA Health Centres guidance describes reception and waiting, consultation areas, staff and support areas, with specialist areas depending on the service plan. Use that framework with your healthcare design consultant; it is not a ready-made layout for every unit.
items: List the planned specialities, consultation and treatment functions, and expected staff needs.
Identify shared rooms and rooms that need dedicated equipment or services.
Record accessibility, privacy and patient movement needs in the brief.
Keep clinical requirements separate from optional decorative finishes.

sections.heading: Build a room-by-room scope before comparing quotes
sections.text: A room schedule connects the operator brief to the fit-out scope. For each room, record the intended use, approved design information, joinery, finishes, equipment interfaces and services. Compare proposals against the same schedule so a missing item does not look like a saving. Final requirements must follow the applicable design and authority review.
items: Reception and waiting: desk functions, seating layout, storage and wayfinding.
Consultation and treatment rooms: the agreed layout, privacy, cabinetry and equipment interfaces.
Support and staff rooms: the functions and storage required by the operator brief.
Services: show which party designs, supplies, installs, tests and signs off each interface.

sections.heading: Separate fit-out work from specialist equipment
sections.text: Do not assume that a fit-out quotation includes medical equipment, specialist systems or their certification. Provide equipment schedules and supplier drawings where available. Confirm power, data, plumbing, ventilation and other interfaces with the appointed designers and suppliers before setting out partitions or producing cabinetry. Room services are project-specific; a reception photograph does not establish what a treatment room needs.

sections.heading: Check the authority route for the actual location
sections.text: Dubai does not have one interchangeable approval route for every healthcare address. DHA guidance describes healthcare facility design and licensing within its jurisdiction, with Dubai Healthcare City identified as an exception. DHCC publishes a separate engineering fit-out process. Confirm the applicable regulator, landlord requirements and appointed qualified healthcare design consultant for the site. FANN is not presented here as a DHA-prequalified healthcare design consultant, a regulator or a guarantor of approval.
items: Confirm the facility type, location and licensing route with the operator and the relevant authority.
Name the party responsible for healthcare design submissions, landlord approvals and fit-out permits.
Keep current approved drawings and revision history available to the site team.
Treat an opening date as a planning target, not permission to start before approvals.

sections.heading: Plan procurement and handover around agreed responsibilities
sections.text: Agree the design information needed before joinery production, the site access conditions and any dependencies on specialist suppliers. For an occupied centre, discuss whether work can be phased and what operational restrictions apply. The programme must reflect the actual scope and approvals; no fixed duration or uninterrupted operation is promised.
items: Confirm drawing release, material samples and equipment interface information before production.
Record working hours, access, protection and waste arrangements with the building team.
Agree testing, inspections, defects and handover documents by trade.
Keep licensing and permission to operate distinct from construction completion.

sections.heading: Looking for medical centre fit-out in Arabic?
sections.text: Common search terms include تجهيز مركز طبي في دبي and تشطيب عيادات ومراكز طبية في دبي. This page is an English operator brief for medical-centre and polyclinic fit-out enquiries. Send the site details and room schedule to discuss the proposed work.

They are references for discussing interior preferences, not claims of sole design ownership, sole contractor responsibility, measured clinical outcomes or authority approval. The scope proposed for your centre will be confirmed separately.

faqs.question: What is different about a medical-centre fit-out brief?
faqs.answer: A multi-room centre needs a clinical service plan, room schedule and clear responsibilities for shared spaces, services and specialist equipment. Start with those requirements before comparing finishes or headline prices.

faqs.question: What should I send FANN for a medical-centre fit-out enquiry?
faqs.answer: Send the site location, available drawings, planned services, room list, equipment information, current approval status and target opening date. Identify the operator and appointed design consultant so the proposed construction and joinery scope can be defined.

faqs.question: Does this page promise DHA approval?
faqs.answer: No. Approval and licensing depend on the facility, location and applicable authority requirements. The operator should confirm the route and appoint the qualified specialists needed. FANN is not described here as a DHA-prequalified healthcare design consultant or an approval guarantor.

faqs.question: Is Dubai Healthcare City handled in the same way?
faqs.answer: Do not assume so. Dubai Healthcare City publishes its own engineering fit-out process, while DHA healthcare facility guidance identifies DHCC as an exception to its jurisdiction. Confirm the current regulator, building and fit-out requirements for your address.

faqs.question: Are medical equipment and specialist systems included?
faqs.answer: Only if the agreed proposal specifically includes them. Record design, supply, installation, testing and certification responsibilities for equipment and services separately from general fit-out and joinery.

faqs.question: Can I see real healthcare project photographs?
faqs.answer: Yes. This page links to Aspris Clinic - City Walk and Fayy Health Polyclinic in the FANN portfolio, with real project galleries. The photographs are interior references, not proof of sole design or contractor responsibility.

faqs.question: How much does a medical-centre fit-out cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: There is no single price on this page. Location, room functions, existing condition, equipment interfaces, finishes and the agreed responsibilities affect the scope. Compare itemised proposals against the same drawings and room schedule.

The brief starts from your confirmed allocation and exhibitor manual, moves through 3D design visuals, and continues into fabrication at our Umm Al Quwain workshop, delivery, installation and dismantling. sections.heading: Start from the allocation and the exhibitor manual
sections.text: Every stand at Dubai World Trade Centre is governed by the show's exhibitor manual: build-up and dismantling windows, submission deadlines for drawings, height limits and service order cut-offs. Send us the hall and stand number, dimensions, open sides and the current manual. Public show dates are not build-up, submission or dismantling deadlines; those come from your manual.
items: Allocation: hall, stand number, dimensions, open sides and any adjoining structures.
Submissions: stand drawings and risk documents to the organiser or venue by the stated deadline, with a named owner on our side.
Deadlines: service orders and approval submissions carry their own cut-off dates, separate from the show dates.

sections.heading: Venue services and appointing your own contractor
sections.text: Utilities, rigging and venue services at DWTC are ordered through the organiser's official manuals and order forms, with early-order deadlines. Exhibitors with space-only allocations commonly appoint their own stand contractor for a custom build; confirm the current rules, nomination forms and any venue approval steps for an independent contractor in your exhibitor manual. FANN works to whichever appointment route your show requires.
items: Utilities and services: power, water, compressed air, internet and rigging via the official order forms, with early-bird deadlines.
Rigging and overhead structures: only with venue approval and certified rigging points; plan loads and drawings early.
Double-deck stands: possible in principle, subject to venue approval, structural drawings and the manual's conditions.

sections.heading: Built in our own workshop, installed by our own team
sections.text: FANN takes the agreed design into fabrication in our Umm Al Quwain workshop, then logistics, installation and dismantling at DWTC. You get one scoped contract and one accountable team from concept to handover, with the itemised scope in writing before work begins.

faqs.answer: Yes. We design, fabricate and install custom exhibition stands at DWTC as an independent Dubai contractor. The appointment route and any nomination forms come from your show's exhibitor manual; we work to whichever route the organiser requires.

faqs.question: What should I send for a DWTC stand proposal?
faqs.answer: Send the show name, hall and stand number, dimensions, open sides, planned products and activities, brand assets and required dates. Include the current exhibitor manual and any floor plan or drawings already available.

faqs.answer: Double-deck structures are possible in principle, subject to venue approval, structural drawings and the conditions in the exhibitor manual. We prepare the drawings and manage the submission when the design calls for a second level.
